input.label: SUPPORTED

supporting_evidence.quote: iPhone net sales increased during the first quarter of 2026 compared to the same quarter in 2025 due to higher net sales of Pro models.

input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, the conclusion remains SUPPORTED. 

H1 challenged whether iPhone net sales actually increased in Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025. This challenge is REFUTED by evidence E8 and E1, which show iPhone net sales were $85,269 million in Q1 2026 (ended December 27, 2025) compared to $69,138 million in Q1 2025 (ended December 28, 2024), representing a 23% increase. The numeric check also confirmed this increase.

H2 challenged whether other factors (pricing, currency, non-Pro models) contributed to the increase. The retrieved evidence (E13, E14, E15) discusses general foreign exchange impacts and pricing strategies but provides NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE specifically about whether these factors drove the iPhone revenue increase in Q1 2026. The absence of such evidence does not challenge the claim.

H3 challenged whether non-Pro models were also a significant driver. The retrieved evidence (E16, E17, E18) discusses other periods or general iPhone sales but provides NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE about non-Pro model performance specifically in Q1 2026. Again, absence of evidence does not support this challenge.

The original evidence E1 explicitly states the causal attribution: iPhone net sales increased "due to higher net sales of Pro models." No contradicting evidence was found, and the challenges were either refuted or lacked supporting evidence. The verdict remains SUPPORTED.
